title: Life of a New Item
instruction: A product goes live today with zero interactions. Put its first days in order.
steps: It arrives with a title, description, tags and photos, but no clicks
A content model places it next to similar, well-known items
It is shown to fans of those similar items, within a small exploration budget
The first clicks, saves and purchases come in
Collaborative signal takes over as behaviour accumulates
why: Collaborative filtering is blind here: nobody has interacted with the item, so it has no co-interactions.
Bridge 1: similar by what it IS, not by who clicked it.
Bridge 2: a capped number of fair showings buys honest signal without flooding feeds with an unknown.
Each early interaction turns the item from guessed into known.
The handoff: weight shifts from content to behaviour as the data arrives.
debrief: Collaborative filtering can't see an item nobody has touched. Two bridges carry it across: content similarity (where it belongs) and a small exploration budget (its first real interactions).
